subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a rejectable Plugin SDK configuration-write hook, and which trusted mutation paths and failure semantics should be part of its permanent contract?
rationale: The request adds a durable SDK capability on a security-sensitive control plane; existing validation solves schema and SecretRef failures but cannot choose the plugin trust, ordering, timeout, recursion, and fail-open/fail-closed policy.

options.title: Design a shared pre-persistence SDK hook
options.body: Define a typed hook covering the intended OpenClaw-owned writers after core validation and before atomic persistence, with explicit timeout and rejection semantics.

options.title: Keep core validation only
options.body: Retain schema, SecretRef, hash, and agent-tool safeguards while external validators remain voluntary wrappers rather than mandatory policy.

options.title: Start with a narrow Gateway-RPC seam
options.body: Expose a bounded hook for config.set, config.patch, and config.apply first, then decide separately whether CLI and other mutation paths join the contract.

recommendation.title: Design a shared pre-persistence SDK hook
recommendation.body: Define a typed hook covering the intended OpenClaw-owned writers after core validation and before atomic persistence, with explicit timeout and rejection semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion already identifies steipete as the reviewer who kept the API question open and tied it to the RFC direction.
